Definition: probably from G714; a bear (as obstructing by ferocity):--bear.
BiblicalUsage: The bear appears once, in John's vision of the beast from the sea, whose feet were as the feet of a bear. The Greek text behind the King James reads the bear here, while the later Greek text reads the genitive of a different bear-word, so the verse stands on the Textus Receptus reading.
TheologicalSignificance: One mention of a bear's feet carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the picture, that the beast is a mixture of creatures, strong and shambling and made to be feared.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
